## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(magrittr) # needs to be run every time you start R and want to use %>%
library(dplyr)    # alternatively, this also loads %>%
library(readxl)
library(ggforce)
library(ggrepel)

data = read_excel("2875_subcellular_localisation_withannotations_Fri.xlsx")
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
# Plotting pie chart by logFC - by positive and negative, then as nucleus or cyto

# Define a function to test for keywords across multiple columns
categorize_annotations <- function(row) {
  combined_text <- paste(row$UniProt_Annotations, row$GO_Annotations, row$jensentableoutput, sep = " ")
  case_when(
    grepl("nucl|chromatin|chromosome", combined_text, ignore.case = TRUE) & 
    grepl("cyto", combined_text, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "nucleus and cytoplasm",
    grepl("nucl|chromatin|chromosome", combined_text, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "nucleus",
    grepl("cyto", combined_text, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "cytoplasm",
    grepl("secreted | extracellular", combined_text, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "secreted or extracellular",
    TRUE ~ "other"
  )
}

data <- data %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(group = categorize_annotations(cur_data_all())) %>%
  ungroup()

# Split data into positive and negative log2fc
positive_data <- data %>% filter(log2FC > 0)
negative_data <- data %>% filter(log2FC < 0)

# Function to create pie chart data
create_pie_data <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    count(group) %>%
    mutate(percentage = n / sum(n) * 100)
}

# Create pie chart data for positive and negative subsets
positive_pie <- create_pie_data(positive_data)
negative_pie <- create_pie_data(negative_data)





# Set up a layout with enough space for both pie charts
par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) #, mar = c(5, 5, 2, 2))  # Adjust margins to prevent cutting off

# Function to wrap text for pie chart labels
wrap_labels <- function(labels, width = 10) {
  sapply(labels, function(x) paste(strwrap(x, width = width), collapse = "\n"))
}

# Rqadius of 1 and cex of 0.5 is best - to not overlap the labels

# Positive log2fc pie chart
positive_labels <- wrap_labels(paste0(positive_pie$group, " (", round(positive_pie$percentage, 1), "%)"), width = 12)
pie(positive_pie$percentage, 
    labels = positive_labels,
    main = "Positive log2fc",
    col = rainbow(length(positive_pie$group)),  # Optional: add color to the pie chart
    cex = 0.7,  # Reduce label size further
    radius = 0.5)  # Move labels further out

# Negative log2fc pie chart
negative_labels <- wrap_labels(paste0(negative_pie$group, " (", round(negative_pie$percentage, 1), "%)"), width = 12)
pie(negative_pie$percentage, 
    labels = negative_labels,
    main = "Negative log2fc",
    col = rainbow(length(negative_pie$group)),  # Optional: add color to the pie chart
    cex = 0.7,  # Reduce label size further
    radius = 0.5)  # Move labels further out

# Adjust title size and margins
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))  # Increase top margin for title space
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
# Filter rows where the group is "other"
other_group_data <- data %>% filter(group == "other")

# View the table of rows in the "other" group
print(other_group_data)

# Optionally, save this data to a CSV file
write.csv(other_group_data, "other_group_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}


# Create pie chart data for positive subset
positive_pie <- create_pie_data(positive_data)

# Plot pie chart using ggplot2
# ggplot(positive_pie, aes(x = "", y = percentage, fill = group)) +
#   geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
#   coord_polar(theta = "y") +  # Convert to pie chart
#   theme_void() +  # Remove axis
#   geom_text_repel(aes(y = angle, label = paste0(group, "\n", round(percentage, 1), "%")), 
#             position = position_nudge(y = 0.05),  # Adjust label's position further out
#             size = 4, color = "black") +
#   ggtitle("Positive log2fc Pie Chart") +
#   theme(legend.position = "none")  # Optional: Remove the legend

ggplot(positive_pie) + 
  aes(x = "", y = percentage, fill = group) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +  # Convert to pie chart
  theme_void() +  # Remove axis
  geom_text_repel(aes(y = angle, label = paste0(group, "\n", round(percentage, 1), "%")), 
            position = position_nudge(y = 0.05),  # Adjust label's position further out
            size = 4, color = "black") +
  ggtitle("Positive log2fc Pie Chart") +
  theme(legend.position="none")

```
